introduction: “We should speak as if we are investigating the truth.” The guide collects what the writings say about the manner of teaching: humility, kindliness, no sense of superiority, deeds before words, and, when a hearer refuses, no contention but a prayer and a quiet withdrawal. Paul’s pastoral letters give the same rule, “gentle unto all men, in meekness instructing”; the Qur’an sends Moses to Pharaoh with “a gentle word”; Socrates and Franklin made a method of not asserting. Jeremiah’s fire and hammer, and the dust shaken from the apostles’ feet, are scripture’s reminders that prophets were not always mild.
questions: Is “speaking as if we are investigating the truth” honest for someone who is already convinced?
Why would humility make a teacher more persuasive? Is that a good reason to be humble?
Reading 13 says to leave the unresponsive hearer to himself. What makes that hard?
When, if ever, is the prophet’s fire the right tone?

outside.why: Deal with people in utmost humility, counting them members of one’s own family. In lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
Speak as if investigating the truth together. Socrates: I neither know nor think that I know.
Franklin made it a rule to forbear all direct contradiction to the sentiments of others, and all positive assertion of his own.
“Thou seest my weakness and lowliness.” My strength is made perfect in weakness.
Meeting the proud with kindness. Moses and Aaron were sent to Pharaoh with the instruction: speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed.
Teaching now is through deeds. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
With wisdom, amiability and kindness. The servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves.
Even the Afnáns must show complete meekness. If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.
One who has received a gift invites his friends to share it. Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, we have found the Messias.

The teacher must be enkindled, his utterance like a flame. Jeremiah’s word was a fire and a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces, and he was not gentle. Can a speaker be both the flame of reading 10 and the fellow inquirer of reading 2?
Forbearance towards one who cannot grasp a truth. Restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.
If you possess a jewel others lack, share it in kindliness. Be ready always to give an answer, with meekness and fear.

If the hearer refuses, leave him to himself and pray for him. Jesus told the Twelve to shake off the dust of their feet as a testimony against the house that would not hear. What is the difference between that gesture and the reading’s?
The Qur’an’s formula for parting without contention: unto you your religion, and unto me my religion.
